### CR-020 — Fleet, scale, Gulf admission, the Depression and Keawe

**Register status:** `approved_narrative_directions_integrated_model_estimates_separate`

- A1: HMS Dreadnought (1906) is a non-event for Pacifica, which has had oil-fired turbine destroyers since the 1890s.
- A2: Keawe is recast from labour organizer to environmental engineer. His achievement is a sustainable, beautiful, Singapore-style buildout of Thalassia and the islands, with win-win reforms.
- A3: Labour registration is left out of the main narrative.
- A4: Gulf Republic admission is an open challenge, not an event in the novel. Pacifica demands parity in the Defense Law examination (95%) and in infant mortality (1.05), held for a generation, and is in no hurry. The model keeps a switch for testing.
- A5: Pacifica_financial_model_1846-1932.xlsx replaces Sol's CR-018/CR-019 workbook as the working model. Its numbers stay MODEL estimates.
- A6: The author's decisions on OPEN-020-01 to -23 of 19 October, as recorded in section E. The main ones: the Gulf's admission as an open challenge; a Crown share of 25% in chartered industries and 8% elsewhere; Pacifica Steel buys Carnegie Steel in 1901; the Union responds from 1903 and builds three more capital ships from 1927.
- B1: Oil and turbine programmes carry through fleet classes: turbine destroyers from 1894, cruisers 1898, capital ships 1903; submarines 1900, carriers 1922. Dreadnought answers Pacifica. 1919 combined parity, 1920–22 disposals, 1927 Union additions and 1932 Union accession govern the naval arc; exact ship counts are MODEL.
- B2/B12–B15: Dominance rests on industry, finance, fuel, sea power, standards and institutions. The whole order overtakes the Union from about 1927 through partner growth. Pacifica alone stays smaller before the crash; the 1932 money crossing is a press headline while the Union remains larger in real output.
- B3/B14: Russia’s indemnity eases Japanese war debt; earthquake and bank-crisis costs scale with a richer Japan. San Francisco supplies Japan’s 1927 crisis borrowing. Final B14 supersedes B3’s earlier eighty-percent share and debt scale; all amounts and ratios stay MODEL.
- B5: Admission requires five general measures against the weakest former-territory state, examination parity at 95% of the white rate and infant-mortality parity at a maximum ratio of 1.05, including Black citizens and tribal freedmen; statistical coverage at least 90%, fiscal quota/debt discipline, common standards, examination office/franchise and common foreign policy are binding.
- B5/E1–4: All measures must hold for twenty-five consecutive years, with a second generation at Pacifica’s discretion. General measures pass in 1925 and narrowly through the 1927 flood; the 1931 oil glut breaks the streak. Parity is still unmet in 1932. The Gulf ends an ally and protégé, outside membership; earliest conceivable admission is mid-1960s.
- B5: Gulf oil pays for schools, health, registration, peonage/convict-leasing reform, the 1916 Sequoyah freedmen settlement and the parity campaign. Hoover runs 1927 flood relief; planters holding refugees in camps are prosecuted and the numbers stay honest. Huey Long loses his examination-franchise campaign; Black leaders divide over the bargain.
- B6: The Union’s German private lending, not a reparations loop, drives its worst financial exposure. Pacifica restrains the boom, lends rather than hoards gold, supports banks, raises neither tariffs nor taxes and restructures war debts. Hoover’s Pacifican June 1931 moratorium and the adjustable 1932 gold-dollar order govern the response. The Gulf oil compact is delayed until 1932.
- B7/E7–8: Keawe Kahananui is born in Hilo in 1895, Hapa, to a Hawaiian harbour pilot and a Japanese-Pacifican farming family in Waimanu. Navy fireman at seventeen, examination-made engine-room officer, convoy veteran and environmental engineer; former strikes, labor charter and separate port/bauxite dispute are removed.
- B7/E7: Thalassia is on Kāneʻohe Bay, windward Oʻahu. Keawe’s Living Bay of 1919–23 diverts sewage beyond Mōkapu, protects slopes and restores Heʻeia and other fishponds. Marine reserve and Moku o Loʻe station in 1923; Crown Prince Hirohito dives once in 1921; later zoologists exchange specimens and work at Hayama. CR-021 revision 8 is now supplied and governs constitutional and dynasty details.
- B7: Hilo works 1923–27, family estrangement over forest grazing, ahupuaʻa planning, 1928 Thalassia Plan, public leasehold and published islands index lead to the 1931–32 Waimanu power-price dispute. Refinancing substitutes for the dam; a naval reef-cut compromise has a cost. Kaiulani brokers the Lands and Waters Charter and Keawe joins the hydro board.
- B8/E6/E9: From 1880 the Development Fund invests 70% of surpluses before debt repayment, development bonds and reserves above the crisis buffer. Standing public debt and a state savings/development bank finance industry; the bank is narrative financing, not an extra model growth uplift.
- B9/E10–13: Polytechnic talent and patents grow private national champions. Crown equity is 25% in chartered/concession industries, 8% plus a golden share in competitive industries, zero in banking. Tesla arrives 1884, Steinmetz and Baekeland 1889; a Pacifican engineer and firm open the 1911 moving line. Pacifica Steel buys Carnegie in 1901 and becomes the first billion-dollar company, provoking Union resentment.
- B9/E12: The AC standard reaches the Pacific, East Asia, Latin America and Persian Gulf oil coast; general dominance in British India or most of Africa is excluded. Oil, steel, rail/shipping, finance, vehicles, chemicals/drugs, telecom, film, aluminium and aircraft make the productive lead concrete.
- B10–B13/E14/E16: Skilled migration responds to wages and jobs, brings families, diverts European immigration and recruits skilled Asians through universities. The later 0.3%-of-residents ceiling supersedes the earlier 0.2% cap; entry becomes supply-limited late in the 1920s. Population and labor effects remain MODEL.
- B11/E17–18: Guest workers from 1890 have sector quotas, an employer levy, wage and housing protection, three-year contracts/return passage, employer changes after contract and a path to residence. Mention occasionally; permit registration stays administrative background. Lapsed permits export part of the slump’s cost.
- B13/E19–21: Roosevelt begins emulation and containment in 1903 after the Carnegie sale; full force by 1910, continued by Taft and Wilson. Laboratories, central banking, champions, scholarship bonds, citizen taxation, patent licensing and tariffs check the talent drain. Three new Union capital ships follow the 1927 Concord; revanchist 1930s remain beyond the ending.
- B14–B15/E22–23: Japan, the Gulf, Philippine crown and Siberia catch up at differing integration rates. China, Korea and other trading regions grow more slowly; richer markets feed the champions while dependence creates resentment. Keep each sovereign, protectorate, crown and trading perimeter distinct.
- D: Preserved CR-020 case, before CR-021’s updated ratios and reserve/stress amendments: 1929 residents 25.6m plus 1.1m guests; Pacifica GDP $51.6bn, Union $71.2bn, Japan $20.6bn, order $83.9bn (1.18× Union; 1.77× in 1932), output/person present 2.28× historical US. These supersede intermediate tables as MODEL estimates, not census or national-account canon.

### CR-021 — The constitution of Pacifica and the Pacific Concord

**Register status:** `approved_revision_9_author_corrections_integrated`

- A/J: One set of organs, renamed once in 1887. Constitution of the Realm and 124 counties replace Imperial Constitution/states/cantons. Confederation has no common head of state; the Chancellor lapses under the life Providentor and is restored under Regent/Sovereign.
- A/D: 1856 Articles and member residual powers; one-year Article XIV renewals and lawful dissolution/election. 1865 Enabling Law passes by amendment with protected Hawaiian crown, Kuhina Nui and institutions. Life Providentorship is legal; enabling delegation lapses in 1887.
- B/D/K5: 1874 incorporation breaches protected provisions and annexation bar, replaces legislature with appointed Territorial Council and holds crown in abeyance. Hawaii’s Supreme Court voids it; ruling ignored before massacre. 1876 English Schools Ordinance is illegal. 1914 restoration cures politically, not by reversing the judgment.
- B1–B5: Realm residual powers, credit, immigration, force, public land/water/minerals, networks and general codes; counties have enumerated local powers and land tax. Boards choose senators; Commissioners never serve home counties, rotate at least every five years and can suspend an act thirty days for court review. No foreign county debt; domestic debt needs Treasury consent.
- B3–B4/K11: Four county indicators: infant mortality, examination pass rate, revenue/head, order. Chartered after five passing years; administered after three failing years or declared disorder, with board suspension up to five years renewable by Senate. Organic law redraws boundaries without consent; measures grants and ten-year programme lapse/certification make comparison govern.
- A/K6: Senate county seats, up to one-quarter life appointments, twelve Polytechnic and eight aliʻi seats. Polytechnic at Carquinez, General Staff/exams/audit/telegraph estate, chief from three graduate nominees and removed only with Senate consent. Office of Public Measures has twelve-year heads reporting to Senate. Court of the Realm at Monterey, constitutional chamber. Ministers answer to ruler, not Chamber.
- B6/D/K12–16: Dispersed cities: Thalassia government, San Francisco money, Monterey law, Sacramento interior, Carquinez works, Honolulu Hawaiian crown, Pearl Harbor fleet. Confederal Council at Monterey 1856–1885, no rotating seat. Capital decision 1875; fleet works 1875–85, Pali tunnel/channel 1876–82, cable 1879, offices move 1885, named capital 1887. Los Angeles Crown city from 1910; Portland/Seattle/Salt Lake remain ordinary.
- B6/J: Kāneʻohe/Heʻeia Crown precinct on windward Oʻahu, protected Mōkapu burial dunes and working Heʻeia fishpond; capital land stays Hawaiian throne Crown land, premiums to Mōʻī, Hawaiian crown/kuleana custody with ʻAha Aliʻi. Basalt, spoil lime, timber and copper rather than marble; arsenals at Pearl Harbor and Carquinez. Seasonal chambers October–March, ordinances otherwise laid before next session.
- C/K4/9/10/13: English Realm administration; Spanish/Hawaiian entrenched historic-land languages, other county languages granted. Three-language confederal acts. Crown oath/Hawaiian schools restored 1914; Japanese Realm standing 1927 and some trilingual Hawaiian counties 1928; no Chinese county status by 1932. Gulf English with regional French/Spanish; Defense Law test English or Spanish.
- A/C3/K4/R9-07: 1888 plural franchise one to three ordinary votes plus one tongue vote for each certified Crown-listed language beyond English, expressly uncapped. Referendums examined citizens only; multilingual technical entry plus English bridging year; naturalization/civil exam English; interpreted guest contracts and subsidized community language schools retained.
- D/F1: Kaʻanoe (Noe) Ward c.1860 Lahaina, surgeon father and Maui chiefly mother; Queen’s Hospital nurse 1881, Polytechnic physician 1884, Elias’s physician 1885, 1886 health-board director and mother of Julian. Birth/adoption 1886 with written consent and negotiated health board, continuing contact and Hawaiian upbringing. Registers and begun vaccination are her limited real achievement.
- F1: Noe dies autumn 1888 during a typhoid outbreak; official certificate by Kaiulani’s physician, servants allege poison, missing registers return after a month to Office. Loyalists/Silas spread murder claims; no culprit proved. Kaiulani builds measures on the registers, completes vaccination 1888–92, nurses/water/Kalaupapa in 1890s and population recovery about 1895. Emotional motives remain mixed.
- D/F/K2: Julian learns Hawaiian, English, Spanish and Japanese, spends 1905–06 in Tokyo, comes of age 1907 without a crown. 1914 Act of Settlement establishes House, restores Hawaiian crown and proclaims Kamehameha VI; 1915 Realm accession. Succession eldest son, then eldest daughter, else adopted heir with Senate consent. Kahekili / 雷 Ikazuchi is future Kamehameha VII; lost Kalanimoku remains distinct.
- E1/K9: Pacific Concord / 太平洋協約 Taiheiyō Kyōyaku, colloquial Concord/Taihei; la Concordia del Pacífico and ka Lōkahi. The Union always means the United States. Restoration circles use Thalassia bakufu and Taiheiki imagery against the shared government.

- E3/K1/2: Co-equal crowns under alternat; common executive entrusted to Crown of Pacifica for five-year terms 1927,1932,1937 with both crowns’ consent. Japan keeps crown, Diet, cabinet, home army, railways and posts; home army common only in declared Concord war. Sixty delegates per side separately exchange messages, joint vote without debate after three disagreements. Tribunal three judges per side, alternating chair. ### CR-033 — Settlement, Native recovery and the shape of Pacifica's population

**Register status:** `approved_integrated_local_labels_retained`

- The gold rush settles rather than passes through: light licences, assisted passage of women and families, secure titles, Pacific shipping and Americans moving west. About 1.2 million people at the start of 1861 (MODEL).
- No mass killing of Native Californians: disease reduces them to about two-thirds of their 1848 number by the later 1890s, and they grow again under fair treatment, keeping a health gap. Whatever the Republic does for them must also pay for the Republic.
- The Republic is the sole lawful buyer of Native land. Treaties of 1851–52 reserve homelands under a three-part compact: reserved homeland leased only through the Republic, ceded land bought by deed against annuities in goods, and the Republic as trustee collecting rents for a fee with published accounts.
- A Land Fund kept apart from the revenues pledged to London pays the annuities from settlers' instalments; its margin helps pay for assisted passage (about 47% in the workbook). Militia service is paid in land warrants good only on bought land. The public register is the title; old grants are confirmed by survey against a fee in land; squatters buy on instalments.
- Land still leaves Native hands through long leases, assigned annuity claims and court rulings, with a fee to the Realm on every lease.
- Japanese immigration predominates over Chinese from the 1900s; Filipino migration is mostly after 1914. Population figures in the prose follow the workbook of 28 October 2026 (MODEL): about 5.6 million Japanese-origin and 4.8 million Chinese-origin Pacificans and about 36 million people in 1932.

### CR-037 — No cliques: keeping the examination state's institutions open

**Register status:** `approved_integrated`

- Pacifica stops any ethnic or religious group from capturing an institution by favouring its own; the rules apply to every group alike. The test is the examination, never a quota.
- From the late 1870s Soberanes's examinations use numbered, recopied scripts; examiners never judge candidates from their own state or college; first postings are away from home; appointment boards include outsiders.
- From 1888 the Office publishes appointments against the examination lists for every chartered body, college and licensed profession; persistent gaps bring audits; officials declare relatives and former students. The first great audit (1890) falls on an established mixed clique on the savings and development bank's board, and Victoria refuses both to stop it and to set quotas.
- Counties may be culturally concentrated and are measured against their own pass lists. A passed-over rate below two-thirds of the best-placed group over five years, or one family, marriage network or congregation holding more than a third of senior posts, counts against the order standard; treasurer, auditor, examiner and chief of police are posted from outside by the Office, in rotation.
- The Japanese naval party's reserved squadron stays, with its critics, until the 1932 renewal.

**Still open:**
- The Carquinez men (the clique of the examined) and selective enforcement under Julian, for later CRs.

### CR-038 — The machinery's own safeguards

**Register status:** `approved_integrated`

- Retirement at 68 for every senator, judge, county Commissioner, estate head and senior officer; the Constitution sets it for appointed senators and the regency extends it. Only the Crown, the Regent and the Truce's named holders are exempt.
- Vallejo College at Monterey from 1889: one academic year for rising officers of every estate, the navy, the champions and the counties, with no restriction by sex; free choice produces two informal sides, the Presidio (engineering, technology, management; the Carquinez men) and the Kaʻahumanu House (health, welfare, education).
- The Office's unannounced inspectors check county returns against figures hard to fake.
- From 1888, Realm scholarships (five years' work anywhere in Pacifica, League teaching included) and posted grants (five years in the named post only); senior pay set by the Senate against the champions' managers' pay and published.
- County halls under a Realm enabling law, held by an Office inspector and trustees to a central minimum, free above it, fostering cohesion and results-based pride in Pacifica.
- Hawaii abolishes penal labour contracts on joining the Confederation in 1856; works crews hire on fixed terms from the 1860s; the general guest-worker programme stays in 1890.
- A trades congress chartered by law in 1895 keeps funds, the tradesmen's register and a reference wage table; it never hires, trains or pays; independent unions stay legal; guest workers reach it only through its Guest Workers' Aid.

**Still open:**
- A Crown-affiliated party (on hold).

### CR-041 — The Russian war re-planned: one summer, one winter (Plan C), the tri-partite Siberian treaty and the Tomsk vote

**Register status:** `approved_directions_integration_pending`

- Pacifica seizes the Siberian line in one week from 26 May 1918 with the Legion's rising as trigger; no declaration of war; the stated objectives are the Entente's. The recognition of a state of war with the Council of People's Commissars comes in September 1918 after the hostage-taking.
- Kazan is held in September 1918 (second battle, Pacifican river flotilla and a brigade); the Volga is the coalition's line through the winter of 1918–19; the Perm wing reaches Glazov and cuts the Vologda–Vyatka line at Kotelnich in January 1919.
- The Siberian treaty is signed in late July 1918 at Samara and Omsk by Komuch, the Provisional Siberian Government and Alash Orda under Pacifican guarantee, built on Komuch's Alash declaration and the Sapozhnikov–Bukeikhanov draft of 29 July–3 August 1918, printed by the Office and deposited in Peking and Tokyo; Julian ratifies it publicly on 10 September 1918 after the Romanov discovery and the Terror decree.
- Komuch's credit is conditional on enforcing the Constituent Assembly's land law without landlord reclamation. The Omsk coup of 18 November 1918 is attempted and fails in one night; the Directory survives; Kolchak declines the title, refuses the Baltic under Kiyoshi in 1919 and becomes federal Russia's navy minister after Harbin.
- The Red spring offensive of 1919 is spent on the Volga: Vance holds the Volga bridge at Zelenodolsk in June 1919 while the trains clear (replacing the Ob crossing of January 1920, which is deleted). Omsk never falls. Wrangel takes the southern command in October 1919 when Denikin stalls at Orel and takes his guns from the Directory's hand.
- The 1920 sequence is unchanged: Tula in February; Trotsky taken at the Oka bridge at Serpukhov by Kutepov's troops and the armoured train Ofitser; Moscow in March; Petrograd by land; Lenin taken on the Vologda–Vyatka line at the Kotelnich bridge by the Pacifican armoured train Māui; Kronstadt in May (CR-040 K1).
- The 1919 bargain's mechanism: Wrangel's price is the unity of Russia including Siberia; since the treaty is signed, Julian promises to deliver Siberia's own vote and does so in 1921, when the Siberian Regional Duma at Tomsk votes to enter the federal compact under the guarantor's credit, Office and paymaster. Nobody puts the question to Alash: the Alash–Siberia union of 1918 is dissolved and Alash becomes a land of Russia without being asked. Victoria's charge gains the count that he asked one people and not the other.
- Oil: Pacifica keeps the Emba (Dossor) concession from 1918; Grozny and Maikop concessions come from Wrangel's government against the reconstruction credit; Baku is a joint Anglo-Pacifican concession with Azerbaijan under Entente guarantee, Pacifica operating, Britain strategic.
- Kiyoshi's Baltic squadron: Izumo (flag), Nisshin, Akashi, twelve Japanese destroyers retained in European waters in spring 1919, with two Pacifican turbine cruisers, six destroyers, minesweepers, a seaplane tender, motor torpedo boats and a landing force; winter base Reval and Libau; enters the Kronstadt roads at the end of April 1920.
- Southern border shape C: Don, Kuban and Terek as federal lands of Russia; Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan independent under Entente guarantee; Turkestan a federal land of Russia; the eastern Donbas Russian.
- Ballin's death on 9 November 1918 is a one-line beat; no Soviet state survives 1920; Nikolayevsk and the Kamchatka concession stand as drafted.

**Still open:**

- Fact changes deferred to integration (the Fact changes section of CR-041.md): the Omsk coup fails; Vance's stand moves to the Volga bridge in June 1919; no independent Siberia or Siberian Republic after the Tomsk vote. Also CR-040's deferred Kiyoshi-at-Kronstadt pattern.
- Which Ukraine (Hetmanate or Directory) and the Black Sea coast; Bessarabia; Kars, Ardahan and Batum.
- What Alash keeps inside Russia after 1921 beyond courts and the kibitka tax; the fate of its regiments.
- The hostages of 1918: how many railway advisers shot, and the one the reader has met. Who from Thalassia attends the Romanov burial. Where Kiyoshi's sword rests; a death poem. The day of Lenin's capture and the name of the Pacifican commander at Kotelnich. Whether the Tomsk vote is shown or reported.
- VERIFY before integration: Legion day-dates for Omsk, Samara, Krasnoyarsk and Vladivostok; Kolchak's October 1917 departure from San Francisco; the Tomsk Duma dispersal of 26 January 1918; Ironside's Kotlas plan; the Red recapture of Ufa on 9 June 1919; the Romanov Bridge name; Mikhailov's role in the coup; Boldyrev's refusal of Kolchak; Krivoshein in Kyiv in late 1918; the Provisional Siberian Government's declaration of 4 July 1918.

### Author-approved editorial safeguards

- Do not give the dead legitimate child no individuality; portray him as a real person before the accident.
- Do not make infertility or jealousy the sole motive for Victoria's subsequent decisions.
- Do not reduce the younger mother to a reproductive plot device; she must have her own agency.
- Do not assert Victoria murdered Julian's mother without deliberate later authorization; preserve genuine ambiguity.
- Do not make Julian's later politics genetically or psychologically inevitable, or predetermine his character.
- Preserve Victoria's independent statecraft, political ambitions, and complicity in imperial decisions.
- No technological miracles or effortlessly incompetent opposition.
- Authorial change requests are authoritative; editorial implementations beyond them remain proposals.
- Keep the current master storyline a continuous affirmative narrative, without comparisons to old manuscript construction; put research and implementation notes in historical_background.md.
- Distinguish verified historical events from fictional divergences, particularly Pico-Castro reconciliation, spring 1846 convention, Sloat's delayed response, British debt support and the lawful Puʻuloa lease and illegal 1874–1876 ordinances.
- Victoria Kamāmalu is historical, born 1 November 1838; the separate Princess Kaʻiulani is born 1875. CT-VICTORIA-KAMAMALU is retired duplicate provenance of active CT-KAIULANI.
- Lot dies December 1872; Victoria succeeds under his designated-heir provision, not an election. Rising and lease in 1874 precede illegal ordinances and 1876 judgment.
- Silas’s late-1851 birth and Kiyoshi’s 1859 birth/spring-1858 conception are settled by the supplied master and CR-027. Kalanimoku’s birth after the November 1858 wedding and later-1870s loss are settled; exact birth year and accident remain OPEN.
- No automatic assumption that Japan's Perry mission vanishes solely because California has purchased coal contracts.
- The 1783 mining ordinances do not settle contested private titles or the rights of Indigenous peoples without state law and negotiation.
- Treat 1858—not 1860—as the date of the definitive Edo Treaty; the March 1860 Kanrin Maru voyage is a follow-up visit.
- CR-014: Lot retains the Kuhina Nui; no missing-office or personal-countersignature mechanism explains confederal ascent. Enabling authority must follow constitutional-amendment procedures and member ratification.
- Demographic, fiscal and military figures in rise_to_power.md are planning assumptions, not verified canon; test them before writing numerical claims as facts.
- Do not treat the source file's self-labeled APPROVED tags as proof of separate author decisions where this turn expressly identifies historical or mechanical exceptions.
- Distinguish adopted framework from unchosen birthplace, exact legal language, electoral events and statutory dates. Weimar provides a structural comparison, not an in-world source.
- Kuhina Nui standing supports participation in regency and succession but does not automatically confer the crown or the later imperial regency.
- CR-015 labels are component-specific. Merging records does not turn PROPOSED detail or unvalidated model figures into approved fact.
- The Power Timeline controls cadence; CR-015 J1 and later explicit decisions control the named corrections. Earlier dated CR-013 planning text is superseded where cross-referenced.
- Distinguish Pacifican core population from Philippine crown, associated Gulf citizens, Chinese revenue administration and sovereign Japanese/Korean partners.
- CR-016: preserve retired CT-MARCUS-II identity as provenance, without active father-son command genealogy or silently remapping legacy profiles to Soberanes.
- CR-018 fixes the stakeholder endpoint and surviving 1932 order; no Julian self-coup, separate 1914 Emperor Kalanimoku, burning Thalassia or Victoria captivity remains active.
- Kalanimoku the lost son and Kahekili / Ikazuchi, the c.1916 heir, are distinct; CT-KALANIMOKU-HEIR is a stable ID, not the current name. Fleet-General Kuroda is Kiyoshi; retain stable legacy IDs as provenance rather than inventing another commander.
- Russia never completes its own Pacific through connection; Japan completes the eastern link and terminal, with Chinese ownership of Manchuria. Northern coastal cession occurs in 1921, not 1899 or 1905.
- CR-019 OPEN items retain their status except OPEN-019-03 (decided), OPEN-019-09 (superseded by CR-020), and OPEN-019-04 (partly resolved by CR-020). CR-018 section N remains wholly proposed under OPEN-018-18, even where CR-019 refers to its suggested archive and death.
- The 1865 armistice/framework and 1867 Western Senate ratification remain distinct. 1919 combined-fleet limits do not create the 1927 common ministries. Victoria is 93–94 in 1932 without a chosen birthday.
- CR-020 E governs its earlier draft replacements; B4 is superseded and B15/D final figures replace intermediate model tables. MODEL values never become narrative canon through this merge.
- No Gulf membership by 1932, no three-year admission period, no Keawe strike/labor-charter arc or main-story labor registration. Guest permits remain background administration.
- The 1932 Gulf oil compact follows the failed 1931 streak, despite older 1931 compact assumptions in source B6/D. B14’s full 1927 Japanese crisis borrowing supersedes B3’s earlier 80% figure.
- Replacement workbook checks are reported source results. Its missing bank-by-bank and transport tests remain audit gaps, not resolved failures in the earlier workbook.
- CR-021 revision 8 and final K decisions override earlier PROPOSED/OPEN labels inside that attachment. All seventeen OPEN-021 entries are decided; uncapped tongue votes are an express direct author decision in revision 9.
- Julian is never styled President; the presidency is a delegated executive function of his Crown. Hayama always hosts the crowns’ Council; reigning Hirohito never visits Thalassia. The Altai secret is withheld.
- Noe’s identity, 1886 hānai bargain and official autumn 1888 typhoid account are settled; no culprit is proved. Do not erase medical work or reduce Victoria’s rivalry to jealousy.
- Hawaiian Crown land and ʻAha Aliʻi custody are distinct from Realm regulation and county lease administration. The 1914 Act joins crowns and restores legislature and language without reversing the 1876 judgment.
- The latest dominance/reserve/stress comparisons are source-reported MODEL values. Do not mix their Union per-person comparator with CR-020’s historical-US comparator or infer a complete new GDP series.
- Revision 9: Chichibu is selected, not a candidate. His Pacifican education, Crown honors and outdoorsman reputation show Japan’s Pacifican orientation instead of a British/European career. Avoid inventing particular orders, ranks or summit records.
- Nikolayevsk joins Kamchatka and Okhotsk coast as Siberian sovereign territory in 1921. Japanese access requires treaty and creates no automatic base or ownership.
- Dawes chooses the rescue/association; Young campaigns for acceptance and endorses as president-elect. Crowns agree renewal at Hayama, ministers sign/exchange at Thalassia.
- Foreign Affairs and Finance normally Pacifican is a convention, not a statutory nationality rule; only the at-least-one Japanese minister floor is legal. Reserved squadron ends in 1932.
- Noe’s official typhoid account and poisoning testimony remain genuinely unresolved; no culprit is newly selected.
- CR-027 replaces fictional Kaiulani with historical Victoria Kamāmalu while retaining stable ID CT-KAIULANI and all legacy profiles. Historical Princess Kaʻiulani, born 1875, is separate.
- CR-027: No massacre or Hawaiian throne abeyance. The lease is legal; later ordinances and appointed Council illegal; ignored judgment is 1876. The 1914 Act joins crowns.
- CR-027 A22/A27 and the individual B9 echoes remain PROPOSED; A13 approves the settlement’s shape while instrument dates and wording remain PROPOSED. Section D’s questions are not resolved by publication.
- 23 October integration: source instructions and workbook Canon/Approved metadata do not independently authorize new canon. Preserve local PROPOSED/OPEN/MODEL scopes. Missing CR attachments remain absent originals; excerpt records are clearly identified.
